choice.basis: The dashboard shows May's bar as the clear visual outlier, sitting just above the x-axis baseline and far below the lowest printed 10,000 kWh gridline, while the other five months range from roughly 17,500 to 40,000 kWh. This extreme, isolated low value is the defining feature of a critical low-usage anomaly. The chart and form fields print no numeric threshold, baseline, or routing legend that would define 'standard' versus 'critical' low usage, so the decision must rest on the severity of the deviation itself. Record r1's standard-follow-up reading is supported only by the absence of a printed rule; record r2's critical-escalation reading is marked 'unclear' for the same reason. Because the visual evidence shows an order-of-magnitude drop relative to every other month, the anomaly is severe enough to warrant escalation rather than routine handling.
choice.option_label: Escalate May to critical low-usage anomaly review
